name: Gemcitabine + CISplatin (UK-ABC-02)
disease: Biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer)

biomarkers.note: The cisplatin/gemcitabine cytotoxic backbone is NOT biomarker-restricted. Biliary molecular targets - FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, IDH1 mutation, HER2 (ERBB2), BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, and NTRK fusions - are tested to guide targeted or immunotherapy options (predominantly in the subsequent-line setting), not to select or gate the gemcitabine/cisplatin backbone. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Biliary Tract Cancers v1.2026, Targeted therapy (BIL-C 3 of 5) and Principles of Molecular Testing; DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 37 (FGFR2 and IDH1 are the most advanced targets, more common in intrahepatic CCA).

lineOfTherapy: first-line for locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic biliary tract cancer (category 1); also an Other Recommended adjuvant option. Not line-scoped when used as adjuvant therapy.

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate renal function and fitness for cisplatin and hydration. If the patient is ineligible for cisplatin, carboplatin may be substituted.
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (BIL-C 1 of 5 and 2 of 5), footnote g (carboplatin substitution if cisplatin-ineligible)

drugs.name: Gemcitabine

provenance.locator: lines 114827 to 114828 (Ch. 37 Systemic Therapy for Cholangiocarcinoma: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 with cisplatin 25 mg/m2, both IV on days 1 and 8 every 21 days, max 6 months; UK-ABC-02)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 37, lines 114827 to 114829 (UK-ABC-02). Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle.

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.locator: lines 114827 to 114828 (Ch. 37: cisplatin 25 mg/m2 with gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2, both IV on days 1 and 8 every 21 days; UK-ABC-02)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 37, lines 114827 to 114829 (UK-ABC-02). CISplatin 25 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle. ISMP tall-man (CISplatin). Requires pre- and post-hydration; monitor for nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy. If cisplatin-ineligible, carboplatin may be substituted per NCCN BIL-C footnote g.

regimen.cycles: up to 8 cycles (a maximum of 6 months of therapy per UK-ABC-02; DeVita lines 114828 to 114829)

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration
premedications.notes: pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration to prevent nephrotoxicity.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: cisplatin is highly emetogenic; give guideline-tier antiemetic prophylaxis before each cisplatin dose.

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: cisplatin-based, high emetogenic risk on days 1 and 8; prophylaxis required.
Cisplatin hydration protocol; monitor renal function, magnesium, and electrolytes.
Audiometry/neuropathy assessment as clinically indicated (cisplatin oto- and neurotoxicity).

monitoring: CBC before each dose (days 1 and 8) - myelosuppression
renal function (creatinine/GFR), magnesium, and electrolytes before each cisplatin dose
peripheral neuropathy and hearing assessment - cisplatin

doseModificationRules.condition: myelosuppression or renal impairment on day 1 or day 8
doseModificationRules.text: Review required; hold or reduce per protocol for cytopenias or rising creatinine. Consider carboplatin substitution if cisplatin-ineligible (NCCN BIL-C footnote g). Physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Ch. 37 Cancer of the Biliary Tree, Systemic Therapy for Cholangiocarcinoma, lines 114827 to 114829 (UK-ABC-02: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 + cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days, max 6 months)

guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (BIL-C): Cisplatin/Gemcitabine (category 1) as first-line for unresectable/metastatic disease (BIL-C 2 of 5) and as an Other Recommended adjuvant option (BIL-C 1 of 5); reference 4 (Valle, ABC-02); footnote g (carboplatin if cisplatin-ineligible). The guideline lists the regimen by name and prints no per-mg dose; the dose is grounded to the DeVita core layer.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for gemcitabine plus cisplatin (UK-ABC-02) as first-line therapy for biliary tract cancer. Serves intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (#23), extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (#24), and gallbladder cancer (#25); diseaseId anchored to cholangiocarcinoma. Every dose is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 37 Systemic Therapy for Cholangiocarcinoma (lines 114827 to 114829): gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 and cisplatin 25 mg/m2, both IV on days 1 and 8 every 21 days, for a maximum of 6 months (modeled as up to 8 cycles). The Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Biliary Tract Cancers v1.2026 Principles of Systemic Therapy (BIL-C) supply the category 1 first-line status, the Other Recommended adjuvant use, and the carboplatin-if-cisplatin-ineligible option (footnote g); the guideline prints no per-mg dose. ISMP tall-man applied (CISplatin). Cisplatin hydration and nephro/oto/neurotoxicity monitoring are carried in premedications, supportiveCare, and monitoring. Biliary molecular targets (FGFR2 fusions, IDH1, HER2, BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, NTRK) are tested to guide targeted or immunotherapy options, chiefly subsequent-line, and do NOT gate this backbone. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
